name.zh: Z1 莱伯雷希特·马斯号驱逐舰

cause.zh: 在‘维京行动’中，遭到德国空军 He 111 轰炸机的误击。被炸弹击中后失去转向能力并偏离航线，随后可能又触及了水雷（或再次被炸弹命中），舰体断裂成两截沉没。
cause.en: During 'Operation Wikinger', she was mistakenly attacked by a Luftwaffe He 111 bomber. After being hit by bombs, she lost steering control and veered off course, subsequently striking a mine (or being hit by bombs again). Her hull broke in two and she sank.

historyNotes.zh: 二战史上最荒诞的惨剧之一。作为德国海军最新的 1934 型驱逐舰首舰，它没有战死在敌人的炮火下，反而死于自家空军的轰炸。全舰 280 余人阵亡，仅 60 人获救。
historyNotes.en: One of the most absurd tragedies in WWII history. As the lead ship of the German Navy's newest Type 1934 destroyers, she did not fall to enemy fire but was instead sunk by her own air force. Over 280 crew members perished, with only 60 rescued.

name.zh: Z3 马克斯·舒尔茨号驱逐舰

cause.zh: 在目睹 Z1 号被炸沉后，试图前往雷区边缘进行救援，但在混乱和规避轰炸机时误入英国新布设的雷区（也有记录称是被德机后续投弹炸沉）。发生剧烈爆炸后迅速沉没。
cause.en: After witnessing the bombing of Z1, she attempted to approach the edge of the minefield for a rescue. However, in the chaos and while evading the bombers, she blundered into a newly laid British minefield (some records suggest she was also sunk by subsequent bombing from German aircraft). She sank rapidly following a massive explosion.

historyNotes.zh: 与 Z1 一起葬身于这场荒唐的行动中，全舰 308 名官兵无一生还。这次事件让希特勒勃然大怒，也直接暴露了战争初期德军跨军种协同作战的灾难性缺陷，促使德军不得不全面修改敌我识别协议。
historyNotes.en: Perished alongside Z1 in this absurd operation, with all 308 officers and men lost. This incident infuriated Hitler and directly exposed the catastrophic flaws in inter-service coordination early in the war, forcing the German military to completely overhaul its friend-or-foe identification protocols.

cause.zh: 在护卫 HX-84 船团时，遭遇火力占据压倒性优势的德国袖珍战列舰‘舍尔海军上将号’。为了掩护船团分散撤退，该舰独自脱离编队，迎着德军的 280 毫米重炮发起近乎自杀式的冲锋。在吸引敌方火力并死战 22 分钟后，舰体被打成火海沉没。
cause.en: While escorting Convoy HX-84, she encountered the overwhelmingly superior German pocket battleship Admiral Scheer. To cover the convoy's scattering and retreat, she broke formation alone and launched a near-suicidal charge into the German 280mm heavy guns. After drawing enemy fire and fighting to the death for 22 minutes, the ship was turned into a blazing inferno and sank.

historyNotes.zh: 二战护航史上最悲壮的传奇之一。这艘客轮改装的战舰明知必死，却用自己的粉身碎骨为 32 艘商船换取了生机。舰长爱德华·费根（Edward Fegen）在战斗中失去了一条手臂仍坚持指挥，最终随舰阵亡，被英国追授最高荣誉——维多利亚十字勋章。
historyNotes.en: One of the most heroic and tragic legends in the history of WWII convoys. Knowing it was a suicide mission, this converted passenger liner sacrificed herself to buy time for 32 merchant ships to escape. Captain Edward Fegen, who lost an arm during the engagement but continued to command, went down with his ship and was posthumously awarded the Victoria Cross, Britain's highest military honor.

battle.zh: 大西洋护航战 (HX-84 船团)

cause.zh: 在班加海峡遭到英国海军潜艇‘锋利号’ (HMS Trenchant) 的伏击。在近距离内被潜艇一次齐射的 8 枚鱼雷中的 5 枚直接命中，舰体燃起大火并严重右倾，在半小时后翻覆沉没。
cause.en: Ambushed by the Royal Navy submarine HMS Trenchant in the Bangka Strait. Struck at close range by 5 out of 8 torpedoes from a single salvo. The ship caught fire, took on a severe starboard list, and capsized and sank half an hour later.

historyNotes.zh: 二战末期被皇家海军在太平洋战场击沉的少数日本主力战舰之一。沉没时它正向新加坡运送约 1600 名陆军士兵。由于命中数枚重型鱼雷且沉没迅速，导致超过 1200 名士兵和船员丧生，是战争末期日军绝望运输线的缩影。
historyNotes.en: One of the few Japanese capital ships sunk by the Royal Navy in the Pacific theater late in WWII. At the time of her sinking, she was transporting approximately 1,600 army troops to Singapore. Hit by multiple heavy torpedoes and sinking rapidly, over 1,200 soldiers and crew perished, epitomizing the desperate state of Japanese supply lines at the end of the war.

battle.zh: 班加海峡伏击战 (太平洋战争末期)

cause.zh: 在阿留申群岛阿姆奇特卡岛（Amchitka）执行巡逻任务时，由于极地海域大雾弥漫、能见度极低且海况恶劣，在夜间水面航行时意外触礁搁浅。在尝试脱困失败后，被船员遗弃。
cause.en: While on patrol off Amchitka in the Aleutian Islands, navigating on the surface at night in dense polar fog, extremely low visibility, and rough seas, she accidentally ran aground on a reef. After failed attempts to break free, she was abandoned by her crew.

historyNotes.zh: 这是极少数无一人伤亡的沉船事件。在冰冻刺骨的阿留申群岛，全体船员在寒风中利用橡皮艇登上海滩，在一个废弃的村庄里靠吃土豆和生火熬过了 6 天，最终被友军的 PBY 卡特琳娜水上飞机奇迹般地全部救出。
historyNotes.en: This is one of the rare shipwreck incidents with zero casualties. In the freezing, biting winds of the Aleutian Islands, the entire crew used rubber rafts to reach the beach, surviving for 6 days in an abandoned village by eating potatoes and building fires, before being miraculously rescued by friendly PBY Catalina flying boats.

cause.zh: 在基斯卡岛（Kiska）外海执行任务时失踪。根据最新战史研究，它在攻击日本货轮‘鹿野丸’号时，被对方甲板炮反击命中指挥塔，随后在紧急下潜中因深度失控而被海水压强压碎沉没。
cause.en: Missing in action while operating off Kiska. According to the latest historical research, while attacking the Japanese freighter Kano Maru, her conning tower was struck by return fire from the ship's deck gun. She subsequently lost depth control during an emergency dive and was crushed by water pressure.

historyNotes.zh: 在失踪长达 60 多年后，其舰长的三个儿子组建了一支私人探险队，最终于 2007 年在基斯卡岛外海深处找到了这艘潜艇的残骸，解开了 70 名美军潜艇官兵长眠水底的历史谜团。
historyNotes.en: After being missing for over 60 years, a private expedition team organized by the captain's three sons finally discovered her wreck in the deep waters off Kiska in 2007, solving the historical mystery of the 70 American submariners resting at the bottom of the sea.

name.zh: 阿伯纳·里德号 (残骸舰艉段)

cause.zh: 在基斯卡岛海域进行反潜巡逻时，不幸触及日军布设的水雷。巨大的爆炸直接将长达 22 米的舰艉彻底炸断沉入海底，导致 71 名官兵落水（其中 22 人随舰艉沉入深海丧生）。
cause.en: While conducting anti-submarine patrols off Kiska, she unfortunately struck a Japanese-laid mine. The massive explosion completely severed the 22-meter stern, which sank to the seabed, sending 71 crewmen overboard (22 of whom perished as they went down with the stern section).

historyNotes.zh: 这是一个极其特殊的地图标记：它不是一艘完整的沉船，而是一块‘断裂的舰艉’。阿伯纳·里德号在失去舰艉后奇迹般地幸存并被修复（最终于1944年在莱特湾被神风特攻队击沉）。这块沉没在极地冰海中的舰艉残骸，于 2018 年被 NOAA（美国国家海洋和大气管理局）的深海考察队发现。
historyNotes.en: This is an extremely unique map marker: it is not a complete shipwreck, but a 'severed stern'. USS Abner Read miraculously survived losing her stern and was repaired (she was ultimately sunk by kamikazes at Leyte Gulf in 1944). This stern wreckage, resting in the icy polar sea, was discovered in 2018 by a NOAA deep-sea expedition team.

cause.zh: 在基斯卡岛外海浓雾中锚泊时，遭到美军潜艇‘咆哮者号’ (USS Growler) 偷袭。在雷达盲区被一枚鱼雷直接命中舰体中部，发生剧烈爆炸并折断，迅速沉没。
cause.en: While anchored in thick fog off Kiska, she was ambushed by the U.S. submarine USS Growler. Struck directly amidships by a torpedo from the radar blind spot, she suffered a massive explosion, broke in half, and sank rapidly.

historyNotes.zh: 阿留申群岛日军 7 艘阵亡战舰之一。咆哮者号在极近距离（不到 1000 米）内对停泊在雾中的三艘日本驱逐舰发起了一锅端式的鱼雷齐射，霰号当场沉没，另外两艘遭到重创，是一次极为成功的潜艇伏击战。
historyNotes.en: One of the 7 Japanese warships lost in the Aleutian Islands. USS Growler launched a devastating torpedo salvo at three anchored Japanese destroyers in the fog from point-blank range (under 1000 meters). Arare sank on the spot, and the other two were severely damaged, making it an extremely successful submarine ambush.

cause.zh: 在阿加图岛（Agattu）以南海域为日军水上飞机母舰护航时，遭到美军潜艇‘海神号’ (USS Triton) 伏击。身中一枚鱼雷后舰体严重倾斜，在短短 5 分钟内倾覆沉没。
cause.en: While escorting a Japanese seaplane tender south of Agattu Island, she was ambushed by the U.S. submarine USS Triton. After taking a torpedo hit, the ship listed severely and capsized and sank in just 5 minutes.

historyNotes.zh: 就在霰号沉没的前一天，子日号也在大雾迷漫的极地海域遭遇了美军潜艇的致命打击。这连续两天的惨痛损失，让日本海军深刻意识到了在阿留申海域进行水面行动面临着巨大的反潜压力。
historyNotes.en: Just the day before Arare sank, Nenohi also met a fatal blow from a U.S. submarine in the fog-shrouded polar waters. These staggering losses over two consecutive days made the Japanese Navy acutely aware of the immense anti-submarine pressure facing surface operations in the Aleutians.

cause.zh: 在前往基斯卡岛运送弹药和补给途中，遭到美军 B-26 掠夺者轰炸机（陆军航空队）的轰炸。炸弹直接命中了其装满弹药的货舱，导致极其惨烈的连环大爆炸，全舰仅有 17 人幸存。
cause.en: While en route to Kiska carrying ammunition and supplies, she was bombed by U.S. Army Air Forces B-26 Marauder bombers. A bomb directly hit her ammunition-filled cargo hold, causing a catastrophic chain of massive explosions. Only 17 crew members survived.

depth.zh: 未知 (基斯卡岛以东深海)

historyNotes.zh: 它的沉没标志着美军在阿留申群岛的空中力量逐渐取得了绝对优势。由于缺乏防空掩护和雷达预警，日军水面舰艇在这种被美国陆航部队完全覆盖的战区中几乎等同于活靶子。
historyNotes.en: Her sinking marked the U.S. military gradually establishing absolute air superiority in the Aleutian Islands. Lacking anti-aircraft cover and radar warning, Japanese surface ships were essentially sitting ducks in a theater completely dominated by the U.S. Army Air Forces.
